content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends intensive glucose control to achieve near-normal blood sugar levels, as this approach has been proven to delay the onset and progression of albuminuria and the decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in individuals with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Research indicates that while glucose-lowering therapies are effective in managing blood sugar levels, their use in older adults and patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) is limited due to the increased risk of hypoglycemia. Treatment strategies should be tailored to the individual, prioritizing hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) targets that can be safely achieved without exposing the patient to the risk of hypoglycemia.
